poi_stops.title: Theodor-Heuss-Brücke / Bismarckplatz
poi_stops.why_good: Central Neckar crossing with bike lanes that drops you straight onto the Neuenheim river meadows.

poi_stops.title: Neckarwiese
poi_stops.why_good: Heidelberg’s big riverside lawn between Theodor-Heuss- and Ernst-Walz-Brücke, with a paved Neckar Valley Cycle Path along the bank.

poi_stops.title: Kiosk do Bairro / Café Bairro Neuenheim
poi_stops.why_good: Neighborhood café stop at the Neckarwiese playground kiosk (and parent café on Neuenheimer Marktplatz) for coffee right on the loop.

poi_stops.title: Philosophengärtchen / Merianausblick
poi_stops.why_good: The iconic castle–Altstadt–Neckar panorama opposite the Old Town; reach via the paved Philosophenweg approach from Neuenheim (avoid the stepped Schlangenweg).

poi_stops.title: Alte Brücke (Karl-Theodor-Brücke)
poi_stops.why_good: 1788 sandstone Neckar bridge linking Neuenheim and the Altstadt — Heidelberg’s most photogenic river crossing for bikes.

poi_stops.title: Heidelberger Schloss
poi_stops.why_good: Red-sandstone castle ruin above the Altstadt; the road climb is steep but e-bike friendly and rewards with terrace views over the Neckar valley.

poi_stops.title: Mannheimer Schloss
poi_stops.why_good: One of Europe’s largest Baroque palaces; the Ehrenhof is the official start of Mannheim’s Rhine–Waldpark bike outing.

poi_stops.title: Wasserturm Friedrichsplatz
poi_stops.why_good: Mannheim’s Art Nouveau landmark and city pin — easy to clip onto the loop before dropping toward the Rhine.

poi_stops.title: Rheinpromenade / Stephanienufer
poi_stops.why_good: Tree-lined Rhine bank through Lindenhof with ship traffic views and continuous bike-friendly promenade asphalt.

poi_stops.title: Waldpark Mannheim
poi_stops.why_good: Mannheim’s green lung of floodplain forest and meadow paths where the promenade turns into quiet park riding.

poi_stops.title: Bellenkrappen (Reißinsel edge)
poi_stops.why_good: Calm Old Rhine arm beside the Reißinsel nature reserve — ride the paved park paths along the water (bikes stay outside the core NSG).

poi_stops.title: PURiNO Strandbad am Rhein
poi_stops.why_good: Italian riverside restaurant on stilts at Strandbadweg 1 — the classic post-ride pasta/pizza stop before spinning back to the city.

seeds.title: Heidelberg foothills — Boxberg, Bierhelderhof & Gaisberg gravel

poi_stops.title: Heidelberg-Kirchheim/Rohrbach Bahnhof
poi_stops.why_good: Rhine-Neckar S-Bahn stop on the Wiesloch–Heidelberg line — ideal Discover staging for riders arriving from the corridor.

poi_stops.title: Boxberg forest roads
poi_stops.why_good: Entry into the Königstuhl massif’s gravel Forstwege above Rohrbach, used by local gravel and MTB loops toward Kohlhof and Gaisberg.

poi_stops.title: Bierhelderhof
poi_stops.why_good: Historic farm-inn on a clearing at ~260 m with beer garden, Hofladen, and a natural mid-loop pause above Rohrbach.

poi_stops.title: Ehrenfriedhof Heidelberg
poi_stops.why_good: Hillside memorial cemetery on the Speyerer Hof / Gaisberg approach, a quiet landmark on the forest-road network.

poi_stops.title: Gaisbergturm & Mammutbäume
poi_stops.why_good: Lookout tower on the 376 m Gaisberg with Rhine-plain views, next to the 1870s sequoia arboretum — the scenic high point of a ~60–75 min foothills spin.
